tasks.title: Transit of HD209458
tasks.statement: A transit of duration 180 minutes was observed for a planet which orbits the star HD209458 with a period of 84 hours. The Doppler shift of absorption lines arising in the planet's atmosphere was also measured, corresponding to a difference in radial velocity of 30 km/s (with respect to observer) between the beginning and the end of the transit. Assuming a circular orbit exactly edge-on to the observer, find the approximate radius and mass of the star and the radius of the orbit of the planet.

parts.question: Find the approximate radius and mass of the star and the radius of the orbit of the planet.

tasks.title: Galaxy in a cluster at z = 0.500
tasks.statement:
Within the field of a galaxy cluster at a redshift of z = 0.500, a galaxy which looks like a normal elliptical is observed, with an apparent magnitude in the B filter mB = 20.40 mag.

The luminosity distance corresponding to a redshift of z = 0.500 is dL = 2754 Mpc.
The spectral energy distribution (SED) of elliptical galaxies in the wavelength range 250 nm to 500 nm is adequately approximated by the formula:
Lλ (λ) ∝ λ4
(i.e., the spectral density of the object's luminosity, known also as the monochromatic luminosity, is proportional to λ4.)

Hints: Try to establish a relation that describe the dependence of the spectral density of flux on distance for small wavelength interval. Normal elliptical galaxies have maximum absolute magnitude equal to -22 mag.

parts.question: What is the absolute magnitude of this galaxy in the B filter?
Can it be a member of this cluster? (write YES or NO alongside your final calculation)

tasks.title: Two solar mass stars proper motion
tasks.statement:
The planetarium program 'Guide' gives the following data for two solar mass stars:

Star 1:
Right Ascension: 14 h 29 m 44.95 s
Declination: –62º 40′ 46.14″
Distance: 1.2953 pc
Proper motion in R.A.: –3.776 arcsec / year
Proper motion in Dec.: 0.95 arcsec / year

Star 2:
Right Ascension: 14 h 39 m 39.39 s
Declination: –60 50′ 22.10″
Distance: 1.3475 pc
Proper motion in R.A.: –3.600 arcsec / year
Proper motion in Dec.: 0.77 arcsec / year

Based on these data, determine whether these stars form a gravitationally bound system. Assume the stars are on the main sequence. Write YES of bound or NO if not bound alongside your final calculation.
Note: the proper motion in R.A. has been corrected for the declination of the stars.

parts.question: Determine whether these stars form a gravitationally bound system. Write YES of bound or NO if not bound alongside your final calculation.
